_comment: Variant of 01 with the CW pump replaced by a long inverting PULSE that the signal DELIBERATELY OVERLAPS. Revised 2026-08-11. Two earlier settings were wrong and are worth recording: dlam=0.1 made both pulses 1.5-2.3 um slivers that crossed the 30 um block without ever bleaching it, leaving a 75%->9% inversion ramp; and pump amplitude 200 with the long pulse over-corrected, bleaching the whole block to 98.8% so that it became transparent and the pump stopped responding to the population at all. amplitude 50 lands at 53% block mean with a gradient (96% at entry, ~23% at the far wall), which is the useful geometry: the entry half has the gain the signal amplifies from and depletes, the far half still holds the N1 that absorbs the pump. source_1.start_time=60 puts the signal peak at t~154, while the bleaching front is still sweeping (it freezes near t~170), so signal and pump coexist in the medium. That coupling is the POINT, not contamination: the signal depletes N3 by stimulated emission, depletion goes as signal INTENSITY, and the extra N1 left behind absorbs more pump -- so the transmitted Ez acquires an A^2, A^4 ... dependence. It is an EVEN-order readout channel by construction, which is what 01 lacks entirely (0.014% of its variance at degree 2, against a 1.8% noise floor).

reservoir._comment: Isotropic dye-doped medium: uniform n=1.5, no LC constants, no relaxation, no lc_fields.npz. Gain via the sted block, inverted by source_pump's single PULSE rather than by a CW pump or a pre-inverted start -- see sted.N1_0/N3_0 below.

sted._comment: 4-level dye starting in the GROUND state: initial_populations = [N1_0, 0, N3_0, 0] = [30, 0, 0, 0], the opposite of 01 which starts pre-inverted at [0, 0, 30, 0]. There is no CW pump here, so the ENTIRE inversion is built by source_pump's single Ez pulse on the absorption line lbdA=0.45, and the signal at lbdE=0.55 (start_time=210) sees only what that pulse left behind as it passed. If a run shows no gain, check pop_monitor's N3(t) actually rises before reading it as physics.

source_1._comment: The reservoir INPUT: plain (non-beam) Gaussian-envelope pulse on the emission line lbdE=0.55, at the LEFT edge of guide_1. source_type is deliberately not gaussianbeam -- that beam type's amplitude is a NO-OP by design (it divides by a norm computed from the SAME amplitude-scaled field, cancelling |E0|; confirmed against MEEP's GaussianBeam2DSource.get_fields), which silently breaks any amplitude sweep. dlam=0.008 gives sigma=18.9 tu, FWHM 44.5 tu = 29.7 um, matching the pump's block-spanning length. start_time=60 -> peak at t~154, inside the pump's 0-202 window, so the two overlap on purpose. The amplitude LIST sets the strip count via return_quadrosource; data_gen replaces it wholesale, so the 2 entries here are only the default.

source_pump._comment: The INVERTING PULSE -- despite the key name this is not a CW pump (01 has that version). Plain Gaussian-envelope Ez pulse on the absorption line lbdA=0.45, launched at t=0 at the LEFT edge of guide_1. dlam=0.005 gives sigma=20.25 tu, FWHM 47.7 tu = 31.8 um in the n=1.5 block, so the pulse spans the whole reservoir; it switches off at t=202. amplitude=50 (not 200) is chosen so the bleaching front STALLS partway and leaves a partially inverted far half: at 200 the block goes transparent and the pump carries no information about the population. Ez is orthogonal to source_1's Ey so the two do not interfere in the FIELDS -- they couple only through the dye populations, which is what makes Ez a clean even-order channel rather than a mixed one. Scalar amplitude keeps it one uniform line source instead of being split into strips.

pop_monitor._comment: Atom-level sensor: saves N(t) for all 4 dye levels over the reservoir; snap_interval in MEEP time units (1 unit = 3.336 fs)

n2f_map._comment_lam: 61-frequency comb 0.4-0.6, matching monitor_1/monitor_2 so all three sensors share one wavelength axis (SimpleSim de2b284: near2far takes lam_range+n_lam like the 1Ddft monitors, EH gains a leading frequency axis).
n2f_map._comment_npoints: Single 1x200 column at x=199.5 um spanning y in [-100, 100]: the generators read EH[-1,:], so one column is all that is used, and the far-field transform cost scales with n_points x n_lam — 1x200 x 61 freqs is affordable where 200x200 x 61 would be hours per sample (the single-frequency 200x200 map was already ~40 min, 2026-07-30). NOTE this is NOT byte-identical to the old 200x200/size-200 map: that one read its last column at x=300; this reads at x=199.5, and the full 200 um y span is kept so the captured angular range is unchanged.

line_snap._comment: Time-domain LINE record at monitor_2's location, all 3 components ({t, Ex, Ey, Ez}, dt=0.1 ~ 5 samples/optical period). Added 2026-08-07 to resolve the cavity's circulating pulse per drive level; picked up into part files as ls_* by data_gen/_gen_common._load_extras.
